frozen_question: Does the Mendes/Djedet Osirian dossier describe a concrete female-shaped or female-function metal cult object associated with the Djed and phallus, and can that object be identified with the Mendes phallus reliquary or with a surviving archaeological artifact?

method_execution.TOPA_SPIDER: primary/near-primary citation chain: pBrooklyn wording -> Meeks -> independent scholarly quotation/interpretation -> Dendera relic geography -> excavation reports and museum records
method_execution.FIVE_D_SPIRAL: lexeme/wording -> date -> geography -> morphology -> ritual function -> material survival -> contradiction return
method_execution.BEETLE_GRAZER: citation-lineage deduplication; Meeks-derived repetitions count as one source family unless independently supported
method_execution.TENET_REVERSE: late Dendera relic processions and material object classes traced backward to the Saite Delta Manual without turning reverse continuity into proof
method_execution.MATERIAL_CONTROL: require an excavated object, museum inventory, inscription, or secure find context before declaring the textual metal matrix physically identified
method_execution.boundary: Research frameworks organize the evidence; only cited textual, museum, and archaeological witnesses carry authority.

papyrus_brooklyn_47_218_84.scholarly_quotation: Les êtres sont placés sur le djed, un vagin en métal près de lui, car les deux soeurs ... sont à proximité du phallus.
papyrus_brooklyn_47_218_84.source: Mathilde Frere 2019 quoting Papyrus Brooklyn 47.218.84 and Meeks, Mythes et Legendes du Delta

primary_wording_lane.date_boundary: Papyrus Brooklyn belongs to the Saite/26th-Dynasty Delta mythographic tradition, centuries before Plutarch; the exact manuscript/source-layer dating remains a separate philological control.

spieser_synthesis.finding: At Mendes the phallus of Osiris is called the copulating Ba and belongs to the divine flesh defined as the male member plus the backbone/spine. It is related to the Djed, while the nearby metal vagina is interpreted as probably a container or vessel with matricial/womb value. The two female guardians Chentayt and Merkhetes are identified with Isis and Nephthys and supply the feminine element required for resurrection.

processional_separation.finding: The same scholarly dossier describes a metal vagina carried in procession in addition to the phallus of Osiris.
processional_separation.inference: The metal female matrix and the phallus are textually separable ritual objects/functions and must not be collapsed into one artifact by default.

dendera_canopic_procession.finding: Dendera Osirian processional theology assigns local Osirian body relics to containers/vessels. Scholarly synthesis of the procession gives the Mendes/16th-nome vessel a ram-headed form with Atef crown for the phallus-and-back relic set.
dendera_canopic_procession.critical_boundary: This relic vessel is not demonstrated to be identical to the metal vagina/matrix mentioned beside the Djed.

early_excavation_report.source: E. Naville et al., Ahnas el Medineh ... with chapters on Mendes, 1894
early_excavation_report.finding: The Egypt Exploration Fund report documents late-19th-century excavation and identification of the Mendes/Thmuis mounds and provides an early archaeological control for the site.

surviving_metal_matrix_search.definition: No current museum or excavation record was located that securely identifies a surviving object as the pBrooklyn 'metal vagina' or female matrix of Mendes.
surviving_metal_matrix_search.boundary: Absence in this search is not evidence of destruction, concealment, or continued secret preservation.

expected_features_if_literal_object_surv: association with Djed, phallus, spine/backbone, Chentayt/Merkhetes or Isis/Nephthys
possible processional fittings, suspension, base, lid, socket or internal cavity
material_target_profile.search_priority: catalogue descriptions and excavation inventories before visual resemblance

cross_gate_with_female_figurines.finding: Independent Ptolemaic Egyptian object classes establish intentional female genital openings and removable phallic components, proving that receptacle/component ritual technologies were physically feasible in Egyptian material culture.
cross_gate_with_female_figurines.boundary: These figurines are not evidence that the Mendes metal matrix had the same mechanism or dimensions.

H1_literal_metal_anatomical_model.prediction: A catalogue, depiction or excavation description should preserve explicitly female/anatomical morphology or terminology.

H2_metal_container_with_uterine_matrix_v.support: Spieser's interpretation plus broad Egyptian equation of womb/matrix with vessel/container semantics.
H2_metal_container_with_uterine_matrix_v.prediction: Object may look like a vessel or reliquary rather than a realistic anatomical model.

H3_same_as_mendes_phallus_reliquary.reason: The textual/processional evidence treats the metal vagina and the phallus as separable, while the Mendes relic vessel has its own ram-headed/Atef identity.

H4_lost_or_unrecognized_catalogued_objec.prediction: Older museum/excavation catalogues may describe it generically as a bronze/copper vessel, anatomical votive, model, socket, cult fitting, matrix, sheath, case or unidentified temple object.

H5_original_biological_phallus_inside_ma.reason: Textual cultic relic language and simulacrum/reconstitution theology do not authenticate biological tissue.

canonical_seal: 𓂸𓂀 THE TEXT GIVES A REAL OBJECT CLASS: DJED, METAL FEMALE MATRIX, PHALLUS, AND TWO SISTERS. THE MENDES RELIC VESSEL IS A SECOND ROLE UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE. SEARCH THE CATALOGUES FOR THE OBJECT; DO NOT INVENT THE OBJECT FROM THE SYMBOL. 𓂸𓂀
